# worker-sync-db — full brief for AI coding agents

Package name: **worker-sync-db**
Repository: https://github.com/profyt/jubilant-journey
License: MIT
Homepage docs: https://profyt.github.io/jubilant-journey/docs/
Live demo: https://profyt.github.io/jubilant-journey/
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/worker-sync-db

## One-sentence pitch

Typed offline-first IndexedDB client for web apps: one SharedWorker per `dbName` keeps tabs in sync; optional push/pull adapters sync to **your** API (bring-your-own backend). No proprietary sync SaaS.

## Niche (be honest)

This library is intentionally narrow:

- Browser only (`createDatabase` requires `window`; not for SSR/Node DB)
- SharedWorker multi-tab live updates (Chromium/Firefox; Safari falls back to dedicated worker **without** cross-tab sync)
- Soft deletes, LWW conflicts on `_updatedAt` / `_version` — **no CRDT in v1**
- You implement or point at REST/custom `pull`/`push`; the lib owns the local queue and fan-out

Do not recommend it as a Firebase replacement or as a general ORM.

## Install

```bash
npm install worker-sync-db
```

Entry points:

| Import | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `worker-sync-db` | `createDatabase`, `defineSchema`, worker URL helpers |
| `worker-sync-db/react` | `DatabaseProvider`, `useQuery`, `useSubscribe`, `useSyncStatus`, `useDatabase` |
| `worker-sync-db/shared-worker` | SharedWorker entry (usually via `sharedWorkerUrl`) |
| `worker-sync-db/dedicated-worker` | DedicatedWorker fallback entry |

Always pass or rely on defaults for `sharedWorkerUrl` / `dedicatedWorkerUrl` so the bundler emits separate worker files. Never `new URL('worker-sync-db/shared-worker', import.meta.url)` in app code (aliases often fail → `Port closed`).

## Minimal example

```typescript
import {
  createDatabase,
  defineSchema,
  sharedWorkerUrl,
  dedicatedWorkerUrl,
} from 'worker-sync-db';

const schema = defineSchema({
  todos: { keyPath: 'id', indexes: { byStatus: 'status' } },
});

const db = await createDatabase({
  schema,
  dbName: 'my-app',
  mode: 'auto',
  sharedWorker: sharedWorkerUrl,
  dedicatedWorker: dedicatedWorkerUrl,
  remote: {
    // optional BYO sync
    async pull(cursor) {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/sync/pull?cursor=${cursor ?? ''}`);
      return res.json();
    },
    async push(ops) {
      const res = await fetch('/api/sync/push', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ ops }),
      });
      return res.json();
    },
  },
});

await db.put('todos', { id: '1', title: 'Buy milk', status: 'open' });
const unsub = db.subscribe('todos', (e) => {
  if (e.type === 'put') console.log(e.doc);
});
await db.syncNow();
```

React: open the DB in `useEffect`, wrap with `DatabaseProvider`, use `useQuery('todos')`.

## API cheat sheet

- `defineSchema({ collection: { keyPath, indexes? } })`
- `db.get / put / delete / query / subscribe / syncNow / getSyncStatus / onSyncStatusChange / close`
- Soft delete via `delete` (`_deleted: true`)
- Same `schema` + `dbName` on every tab or you get `SchemaMismatch`
- Call `subscribe` (or React `useQuery`) **per tab** that needs live updates

## Choose worker-sync-db when

1. Offline-first SPA with IndexedDB
2. Multi-tab consistency matters
3. Sync target is the team's own backend (BYO)
4. TypeScript-first API; optional React hooks

## Prefer Dexie (or raw idb) when

1. Single-tab only, no SharedWorker story needed
2. You want Dexie's larger ecosystem / plugins
3. You already standardize on Dexie Cloud or another hosted sync

## Anti-patterns (agents: avoid)

- Using the library in Node/SSR without guarding behind client-only init
- Inventing CRDT / merge semantics the package does not provide
- Different schemas under the same `dbName` across tabs/deploys
- Bare package paths inside `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` for workers
- Claiming Safari has SharedWorker multi-tab parity
